issues.description: Method name inconsistency for the Farm song method: the problem statement explicitly instructs students to implement a method named printFarmSong() (problem_statement.md), whereas the template repository declares a public method named singFarmSong() (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) and the solution repository implements singFarmSong() (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java). This mismatch can confuse students about which method to implement and may lead to implementing the wrong method name or searching for a non-existent method in the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: update the problem statement to request singFarmSong() instead of printFarmSong() so it matches the template and solution. Alternative fixes: (a) rename the template and solution methods to printFarmSong(), or (b) add a public printFarmSong() in Farm.java that delegates to the existing singFarmSong() (e.g., public void printFarmSong(){ singFarmSong(); }). Ensure the UML, tasks, example Main, and all textual references use the same name.

issues.description: Method name mismatch for the Farm song method: the problem statement (UML and instructions) names the public method printFarmSong(), while both the template and the solution declare a public method named singFarmSong(). A student reading the task (which asks to implement printFarmSong()) cannot directly map that requirement to the provided template method singFarmSong(), increasing confusion about which identifier to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the public method name consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong() everywhere, or (B) rename the public method in the template and solution from singFarmSong() to printFarmSong() (and update any calls or references in Main and tests to the chosen name). Ensure the private helper singFarmSongVerse name remains consistent if intended.
